entities.name: Abraha Francois
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abraha Francois (b. 1965) is an Eritrean Catholic bishop who has served as Eparch of Segheneity in Eritrea, overseeing Ge'ez Rite Catholic communities in a country where the Church operates under significant government restrictions. Ordained a priest in the Eritrean Catholic Church, he was appointed to episcopal office in the early twenty-first century during a particularly difficult period for religious institutions in Eritrea.

Eritrea's post-independence government has imposed severe limits on Church activities, including restrictions on religious education, property, and the movement of clergy. Abraha Francois navigated this environment while attempting to maintain the sacramental and educational mission of the Eritrean Catholic Eparchy, whose faithful practice the ancient Ge'ez liturgical tradition rooted in the Alexandrian Christianity of the fourth century.

His episcopate represents the persistence of Eastern Catholic churches in the Horn of Africa under authoritarian pressure—a contemporary echo of the region's ancient Christian heritage. The Eritrean Catholic Church, though small in numbers, preserves a distinctive synthesis of Semitic liturgical tradition and Roman communion that distinguishes it from the much larger Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church.
